label: Hard Water
cause: Minnesota groundwater is naturally hard. Dissolved calcium and magnesium picked up from limestone and dolomite bedrock stay in the water all the way to your tap.
approach: 10% crosslinked resin trades the calcium and magnesium for sodium ions before water reaches your plumbing. For homes that want scale protection without salt, a salt-free conditioner reduces scale adhesion but does not remove the minerals.
seo_title: Hard Water Treatment in Minneapolis & St. Paul | MSP Pure Water
seo_desc: Minnesota water is hard. See what hard water does to your home and which MSP Pure Water softening system fixes it, with transparent pricing.

label: White Scale
cause: When hard water evaporates or is heated, dissolved calcium carbonate comes out of solution and hardens into chalky white scale on faucets, showerheads, glass and inside water heaters.
approach: Softening removes the hardness minerals so there is nothing left to deposit. Existing scale stops growing and is far easier to clean.

label: Spots on Dishes
cause: Mineral residue left behind when hard water dries on glassware and dishes. Detergent also works less effectively in hard water, so film builds up.
approach: Softened water dries clean. Most homeowners notice the difference on glassware within the first few loads.

label: Dry Skin / Hair
cause: Hardness minerals react with soap to form a film that is hard to rinse away, leaving skin and hair feeling dry and dull. Chlorine in city water adds to the effect.
approach: Softening removes the minerals that cause soap film. On city water, the Jacobi catalytic carbon tank also removes chlorine and chloramine before the shower.

label: Chlorine Taste / Odor
cause: Municipal utilities add chlorine or chloramine to keep water safe on its way through the distribution system. It does its job in the pipes, but the taste and smell arrive at your tap along with it.
approach: The Jacobi catalytic carbon tank is selected specifically because it treats chloramine as well as free chlorine. Every whole-home city system includes it, so showers, laundry and every faucet get treated water.
seo_title: Chlorine & Chloramine Removal for Twin Cities Homes | MSP Pure Water
seo_desc: Why your city water smells like a pool and how catalytic carbon filtration removes chlorine and chloramine from every tap in your home.

label: Iron Staining
cause: Dissolved iron is common in Minnesota well water. It is invisible coming out of the well, then oxidizes on contact with air and leaves orange-brown stains on sinks, tubs, toilets and laundry.
approach: Air-oxidation (AIO) treatment converts dissolved iron into solid particles inside the tank, and Katalox Light media captures them. Heavier iron loads get hydrogen peroxide injection ahead of filtration. A softener alone is not the right tool for real iron.
seo_title: Iron Removal for Minnesota Well Water | MSP Pure Water
seo_desc: Orange stains, metallic taste and iron in your well water. See how MSP Pure Water treats iron chemical-free and what it costs.

label: Metallic Taste
cause: Usually dissolved iron or manganese. Both are common in Minnesota groundwater and both leave a distinct metallic taste long before they stain.
approach: The same oxidation-plus-filtration process that stops staining removes the taste. Reverse osmosis at the kitchen sink polishes drinking water further.

label: Rotten-Egg / Sulfur Odor
cause: Hydrogen sulfide gas, produced by naturally occurring bacteria in groundwater or in a water heater. You smell it most at hot taps and first thing in the morning.
approach: Hydrogen sulfide needs chemical oxidation. Our Iron & Sulfur Treatment System injects hydrogen peroxide ahead of the Jacobi catalytic carbon tank, then softens. It is the one system we install for rotten-egg odor.
seo_title: Sulfur & Rotten-Egg Odor Treatment for Well Water | MSP Pure Water
seo_desc: Hydrogen sulfide is why your well water smells like rotten eggs. See how MSP Pure Water removes the odor and what the system costs.

label: Manganese
cause: Manganese occurs naturally in Minnesota groundwater. It causes black or dark-brown staining and an unpleasant taste, and the Minnesota Department of Health publishes guidance on manganese levels in drinking water.
approach: Manganese is treated alongside iron: air oxidation converts it to a solid and Katalox Light media captures it. Your well test tells us the level and the right configuration. Reverse osmosis adds a second barrier for drinking water.
seo_title: Manganese Treatment for Minnesota Wells | MSP Pure Water
seo_desc: Black staining and manganese in your well water. How MSP Pure Water treats it with oxidation and filtration, plus RO for drinking water.

label: Sediment
cause: Sand, silt and rust particles drawn in by the well pump or shed by aging pipes. It clogs aerators and wears out downstream equipment.
approach: A pre-system sediment filter captures debris before it reaches your softener, media and valves. Recommended on most well installs.

label: Drinking-Water Concerns
cause: Whole-home treatment fixes hardness and taste, but the water you drink deserves a finer barrier. Dissolved solids, residual taste and the cost and clutter of bottled water are the usual reasons homeowners add reverse osmosis.
approach: A dedicated under-sink RO system pushes water through a semipermeable membrane and delivers it to its own faucet. Choose a compact tankless unit with remineralization or the proven tank configuration. Included free with any whole-home system.
seo_title: Reverse Osmosis Drinking Water in the Twin Cities | MSP Pure Water
seo_desc: Tank or tankless reverse osmosis at your kitchen sink, professionally installed. Included free with every MSP Pure Water whole-home system.
